entities.name: Neanthes of Cyzicus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Neanthes of Cyzicus was a Greek historian and rhetorician of Cyzicus in Anatolia, living in the fourth and third centuries BC.

Born around 350 BCE, Neanthes is best known for his work 'History', which chronicled the history of the region from the Persian Wars to the death of Alexander the Great.

The 'History' is notable for its geographic scope, covering the entire region from the Black Sea to the Euphrates River.

Neanthes' work was widely studied and admired in his time, and he is considered one of the most important historians of the Hellenistic period.

Despite its significance, much of Neanthes' 'History' has been lost to time, and only fragments remain.

A striking testament to his influence can be seen in the works of later historians, such as Arrian and Pausanias, who built upon his research.

The legacy of Neanthes of Cyzicus serves as a reminder of the importance of geographic and cultural understanding in shaping our understanding of the ancient world.
